entries.title: Psalms 41:1
segments: This psalm is best explained upon the supposition that David wrote it when he was lying upon a bed of sickness,
.  This encouraged his enemies to form mischievous plots against him,
; though at the same time they paid him hypocritical visits of pretended friendship,

. 
 
  Considereth: has compassion upon the poor, and assists them. David's own condition of distress and weakness seems to have been the occasion of this reflection. 
 
Compassion to the poor and needy, and readiness to assist them for the Lord's sake and in imitation of his example, is an evidence of love to him and preparation for the reception of his mercies.

entries.title: Psalms 41:3
segments: Make all his bed; comfort and support him.

entries.title: Psalms 41:4
segments: The pardon of sin and deliverance from its guilt and power are more to be desired than deliverance from temporal suffering, or the possession of all earthly good.

entries.title: Psalms 41:9
segments: Mine own familiar friend; these words apply to the conduct of Ahithophel towards David, but had their most perfect fulfilment in the treachery of Judas, and were applied to him by the Saviour himself.
Confidence in creatures may be sadly disappointed; but trust in the Lord, and expectation of good from him in the keeping of his commands, will be fully realized and meet an abundant reward.

entries.title: Psalms 41:10
segments: May requite them; in these words David, and in David Christ, speaks as the head and representative of God's church.  It is no private revenge which he desires, but the deliverance of God's people from their malicious foes, who in seeking his destruction seek theirs also.

entries.title: Psalms 41:11
segments: God's faithfulness to his covenant people makes the destruction of their incorrigible enemies necessary and certain.  Though they may triumph for a season, he will manifest his everlasting lovingkindness towards his church in their final overthrow.

entries.title: Psalms 41:12
segments: Settest me before thy face; makest me blessed in thy presence.

entries.title: Psalms 41:13
segments: Amen, and Amen; this doxology marks the conclusion of the first of the five books, or rolls, into which the Psalms have been from ancient times divided.
